stem:
In an experiment on a healthy 26-year-old volunteer, a sustained rise in glomerular filtration rate increases the flow of tubular fluid past the macula densa.

Which of the following sequences most directly restores the filtration rate toward baseline?

options.label: A
options.text: Juxtaglomerular cells increase renin secretion, raising systemic angiotensin II
options.misconception: A slower endocrine pressor pathway is being substituted for the local feedback loop.
options.explanation: Tubuloglomerular feedback acts locally through ATP and adenosine on the afferent arteriole; renin release responds to decreased perfusion, not to an acute rise in filtration.

options.label: B
options.text: Macula densa cells release nitric oxide, dilating the efferent arteriole
options.misconception: The fine-tuning vasodilator is being cast as the primary negative-feedback signal, and at the wrong arteriole.
options.explanation: Nitric oxide relaxes the afferent arteriole and opposes the ATP/adenosine signal; the feedback that lowers an elevated GFR is adenosine-mediated constriction of the afferent vessel.

options.label: C
options.text: Macula densa cells release ATP and adenosine, constricting the afferent arteriole
options.misconception: None; increased distal NaCl and flow trigger paracrine constriction of the afferent arteriole.
options.explanation: When filtration rises, more NaCl reaches the macula densa; the activated cells release ATP and adenosine, which act as paracrine factors that constrict the afferent arteriole, slowing blood flow and reducing GFR.

options.label: D
options.text: Principal cells insert aquaporin channels, diverting water from the tubule
options.misconception: A collecting-duct water mechanism is being credited with changing glomerular filtration.
options.explanation: Aquaporin insertion alters water recovery downstream of the glomerulus; it does not feed back on the filtration rate, which is controlled at the afferent arteriole.

options.label: E
options.text: Sympathetic nerve activity rises, dilating the afferent arteriole
options.misconception: Both the direction of the vascular response and the neural mechanism are wrong.
options.explanation: Increased sympathetic firing constricts, not dilates, renal arterioles; the moment-to-moment feedback to a high GFR is the local macula densa paracrine mechanism.

context: Learning objective: trace tubuloglomerular feedback. High distal NaCl/flow activates macula densa cells to release ATP and adenosine, constricting the afferent arteriole and reducing GFR.
